title: New Study Shows Midlife Health Habits Can Add Years of Brain Health
subtitle: Managing blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking in middle age could delay dementia by over a decade.

summary.en: A large new study reveals that maintaining good vascular health in middle age is linked to a significantly longer life without dementia. Researchers tracked over 12,000 people to see how smoking, blood pressure, and diabetes affect brain health. The findings show that individuals who avoid these three risks at age 55 live an average of 13 years longer without cognitive decline. This research provides a clear strategy for people to protect their brain health as they age. Experts emphasize that these midlife choices are essential for preserving mental clarity in the later years of life.
summary.zh: 一項大型新研究顯示，在中年時期維持良好的血管健康，與更長久且免於失智症的生活有顯著關聯。研究人員追蹤了超過一萬二千人，以觀察吸菸、血壓與糖尿病如何影響大腦健康。研究結果顯示，在五十五歲時避免這三項風險的人，平均能多出十三年免於認知功能衰退的生活。這項研究為人們在老化過程中保護大腦健康提供了明確的策略。專家強調，這些中年時期的選擇對於在晚年保持心智清晰至關重要。

paragraphs.en: A major new study has provided fresh evidence that our health choices in middle age have a powerful effect on our brain health later in life. According to MedPage Today, researchers found that people who avoid three specific health risks during their middle years can add nearly 13 years of dementia-free life to their future. This study offers a hopeful look at how simple lifestyle changes can help people stay mentally sharp for much longer.
paragraphs.zh: 一項大型的新研究提供了新的證據，顯示我們在中年時期的健康選擇，對晚年的大腦健康有著深遠的影響。根據醫學新聞網站 MedPage Today 的報導，研究人員發現，若人們在中年時期能避免三種特定的健康風險，未來將能多出近十三年免於失智症的生活。這項研究為簡單的生活型態改變如何幫助人們長期保持思緒敏銳，提供了充滿希望的觀點。

paragraphs.en: Building on earlier research from August 2026, which first highlighted the link between midlife habits and brain health, this latest report provides more detailed data. The study followed 12,409 participants in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) project, which began in 1986. By tracking these individuals for over 26 years, scientists were able to see how vascular health—the health of our blood vessels—influences the aging process. The researchers focused on three main factors: high blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking.
paragraphs.zh: 這項最新報告建立在二零二六年八月的研究基礎上，該研究首次強調了中年習慣與大腦健康之間的關聯，並提供了更詳細的數據。這項研究追蹤了「動脈粥狀硬化風險社區研究 (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities, ARIC)」計畫中的一萬二千四百零九名參與者，該計畫始於一九八六年。透過對這些受試者長達二十六年的追蹤，科學家得以觀察血管健康（即我們血管的健康狀況）如何影響老化過程。研究人員聚焦於三個主要因素：高血壓、糖尿病與吸菸。

paragraphs.en: According to MedPage Today, the results were clear. At age 55, participants who did not smoke, had normal blood pressure, and did not have diabetes lived an average of 30.1 more years without dementia. In contrast, those who struggled with all three of these health issues at the same age lived only 17.5 years without the condition. This means the healthier group gained nearly 13 extra years of cognitive health. The study also noted that people with all three risk factors were significantly more likely to develop dementia or pass away before a diagnosis could be made.
paragraphs.zh: 根據 MedPage Today 的報導，研究結果相當明確。在五十五歲時，沒有吸菸、血壓正常且未患有糖尿病的參與者，平均能多出三十點一年免於失智症的生活。相比之下，在相同年齡時若同時受這三種健康問題困擾，則僅能多出十七點五年免於失智症。這意味著較健康的一組人多獲得了近十三年的認知健康。研究也指出，同時具備這三項風險因素的人，罹患失智症或在確診前離世的可能性顯著較高。

paragraphs.en: Josef Coresh, a lead researcher from NYU Langone Health, explained that these findings are very important. He noted that about 42% of Americans are at risk of developing dementia at some point after they turn 55. Because of this high number, finding ways to delay the disease is a top priority for doctors and scientists. Coresh stated that people should actively try to avoid these three health risks in middle age as a way to protect their brains for more than a decade.
paragraphs.zh: 紐約大學朗格尼醫學中心 (NYU Langone Health) 的首席研究員柯瑞許 (Josef Coresh) 解釋，這些發現至關重要。他指出，約有百分之四十二的美國人在五十五歲後的某個階段面臨罹患失智症的風險。由於這個數字龐大，尋找延緩疾病的方法成為醫師與科學家的首要任務。柯瑞許表示，人們應積極嘗試在中年時期避免這三種健康風險，以此作為保護大腦超過十年的方式。

paragraphs.en: The study defined these risks in specific ways to ensure accuracy. Hypertension, or high blood pressure, was counted if a person had a reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher, or if they were taking medicine to control it. Diabetes was identified through blood sugar tests or a doctor’s diagnosis. Smoking was based on what the participants reported about their own habits. By using these clear definitions, the team was able to show how these conditions shape the real-world aging process for thousands of people.
paragraphs.zh: 為了確保準確性，該研究對這些風險進行了明確定義。高血壓的判定標準為血壓數值達到一百三十／八十毫米汞柱或更高，或是正在服用藥物控制血壓。糖尿病則是透過血糖檢測或醫師診斷來確認。吸菸狀況則根據參與者自行回報的習慣為準。透過這些明確的定義，研究團隊得以展示這些健康狀況如何影響數千人真實生活中的老化過程。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the main findings, the study also looked at differences between groups. According to MedPage Today, the research showed that women generally lived longer without dementia than men at every level of health risk. There were also differences based on race and genetics, with white participants living more years free of dementia than Black participants, and those with certain genetic markers, known as APOE4 carriers, having shorter periods of dementia-free survival.
paragraphs.zh: 除了主要發現外，該研究也探討了不同群體間的差異。根據 MedPage Today 的報導，研究顯示，在各種健康風險水準下，女性免於失智症的存活時間普遍長於男性。此外，種族與遺傳因素也造成了差異，白人參與者的無失智生存年數多於黑人參與者，而帶有特定遺傳標記（即 APOE4 攜帶者）的人，其免於失智症的存活期則較短。

paragraphs.en: This research is different from previous studies because it focuses on a "time-based" approach. Instead of just looking at the probability of getting sick, the team measured the actual number of years people lived while remaining mentally clear. This helps doctors better understand the balance between living a long life and living a healthy one. The study highlights that these vascular factors are not just about heart health; they are deeply connected to how our brains function as we grow older.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究與以往的研究不同，因為它採用了「以時間為基礎」的方法。研究團隊並非僅觀察患病機率，而是測量人們在保持心智清晰狀態下實際生活的年數。這有助於醫師更深入了解長壽與健康生活之間的平衡。研究強調，這些血管因素不僅關乎心臟健康，更與我們年老時的大腦運作方式息息相關。

paragraphs.en: For many, these results serve as a reminder that the actions taken in middle age are an investment in the future. While genetics and other factors play a role, managing blood pressure, avoiding smoking, and preventing diabetes are steps that many people can take today. As the population continues to age, these findings offer a practical path for individuals to improve their chances of staying independent and mentally active for as long as possible. The researchers hope that by focusing on these three areas, more people can enjoy a longer, healthier life, free from the challenges of dementia.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多人而言，這些結果提醒我們，中年時期的行動是對未來的投資。雖然遺傳與其他因素也扮演一定角色，但控制血壓、避免吸菸與預防糖尿病，是許多人今天就能採取的行動。隨著人口持續老化，這些發現為個人提供了實用的途徑，以提升在晚年保持獨立與心智活躍的機會。研究人員希望透過專注於這三個領域，能讓更多人享受更長久、更健康，且免於失智症困擾的生活。

Researchers found that avoiding smoking, high blood pressure, and type 2 diabetes can add nearly 13 years of dementia-free life. previousArticles.summaryEn: A recent study published in the journal Neurology identifies three key health factors that influence brain health. Researchers found that avoiding smoking, high blood pressure, and type 2 diabetes between the ages of 45 and 65 can delay dementia. Participants without these risk factors lived nearly 13 years longer without the condition compared to those with all three. Experts emphasize that these findings highlight the importance of heart health for brain protection. The research suggests that early management of these conditions is a powerful strategy for long-term health.

quiz.question: According to the study, what is the specific criteria for identifying hypertension in participants?

options.A: A consistent blood pressure reading of 120/80 mm Hg or higher.
options.B: A blood pressure reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher, or the use of medication to manage it.
options.C: A doctor's diagnosis based on blood sugar tests and self-reported health history.
options.D: Any reading that indicates a deviation from the normal range for people over 55.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，研究明確定義高血壓為 130/80 mm Hg 或更高，或者正在服用藥物控制。選項 A 數值錯誤；選項 C 混淆了糖尿病的診斷方式；選項 D 描述過於籠統，未包含文章中提到的具體數值與用藥條件。

quiz.question: Based on the study's findings, what can be inferred about the relationship between vascular health and cognitive longevity?

options.A: Vascular health is the only factor that determines whether a person will develop dementia.
options.B: Improving blood pressure and avoiding smoking are more effective than genetic factors in preventing dementia.
options.C: Maintaining healthy blood vessels in middle age can significantly extend the period of life spent without dementia.
options.D: The study suggests that people with the APOE4 genetic marker cannot benefit from lifestyle changes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章提到血管健康（vascular health）會影響老化過程，且管理好血壓、糖尿病與戒菸能增加近 13 年的無失智生活，顯示血管健康與大腦功能密切相關。選項 A 過度推論，文中提到基因亦有影響；選項 B 文中未直接比較兩者強度；選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到該基因會縮短無失智生存期，未說無法改善。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the author states: 'these results serve as a reminder that the actions taken in middle age are an investment in the future.' What does the word 'investment' imply in this context?

options.A: Spending money on medical treatments to prevent future illness.
options.B: Sacrificing current comfort for a long-term benefit in later life.
options.C: A financial strategy to ensure one has enough savings for retirement.
options.D: A guarantee that one will never develop a disease if they follow the rules.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。此處的 'investment' 是隱喻用法，意指現在付出的努力（如管理血壓、戒菸）如同投資，是為了換取未來（老年）更佳的健康狀態。選項 A 錯誤，文中強調的是生活習慣而非金錢；選項 C 偏離文章健康主題；選項 D 過於誇大，投資不代表百分之百的保證。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: The ARIC project is the most comprehensive study ever conducted on human aging.
options.B: Dementia is an inevitable part of aging that cannot be delayed by lifestyle changes.
options.C: Researchers have discovered that genetics are the sole predictor of cognitive health in old age.
options.D: Adopting healthy habits during middle age can significantly increase the number of years spent living without dementia.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心在於強調中年時期的健康選擇（避免吸菸、控制血壓與糖尿病）能有效延長大腦健康的時間。選項 A 僅是研究背景；選項 B 與文章主旨完全相反；選項 C 忽略了文章強調生活方式對大腦健康的重要影響，而非僅有基因決定。
